stated: Strengthen democratic rights and participation by scrapping the Conservatives’ voter ID scheme and giving 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote in UK general elections and referendums, and local elections in England.

source.quote: Strengthen democratic rights and participation by scrapping the Conservatives’ voter ID scheme and giving 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote. Giving 16- and 17-year-olds the right to vote in UK general elections and referendums, and local elections in England.

bearing_set.reason: Directly affects voting rights and democratic participation: repealing voter ID and extending franchise to 16-17 year olds are core legal/civil rights measures within O9's strict scope.

Voter ID is a compulsory-ID requirement to exercise a civic act; scrapping it removes a state-mandated identity-presentation obligation, directly improving the 'freedom from compulsory ID/licensing' indicator under O10.

membership_note: Two clean bearings: O9 for the democratic-rights and franchise-extension effect; O10 for the removal of a compulsory-ID mandate. No material fiscal, labour-market, healthcare, or other fundamental effects that clear the non-negligible bar.
